resume: Choose a mini-project subject as a group, knowing the approach, the possible data, the deliverables, the schedule, the oral presentation and the assessment.

diapos.sousTitre: Five subjects, six groups, three weeks for a small but complete piece of research
diapos.notes: To be shown at the end of chapter 2: this is when the syllabus plans to hand out the mini-project, for three weeks of supervised independent work. Before the session, set the rule on the number of subjects, the due date, how the work is submitted and the length of the oral presentation, and check that a data source is accessible for each subject. Everything labeled “suggested” comes from the guide and should be adapted.

diapos.titre: A small but complete piece of research
points: Ask a research question
Gather data
Process them in Python
Interpret the results with the critical eye of your discipline
Three outputs: a **notebook**, a **report**, an **oral presentation**
diapos.notes: Present the mini-project as research in miniature, not as a programming exercise. The last step, interpretation, is where literature students have an advantage: the tool produces clues, and it is the research question that gives them meaning.

diapos.titre: One subject or three? The syllabus says both

points: “Work on 1 subject of your choice from” the five subjects
“Mini-project (complete at least 3 of the 5 proposed subjects)”

diapos.notes: The official syllabus gives two different instructions: do not leave the students in doubt. Announce here the rule you have chosen, with your head of department if necessary, write it on the board and keep it all semester. If you choose three subjects, the guide suggests spreading them from week 4 to week 9, one subject every two weeks. If the rule is one subject, you can allow the fastest groups to work on a second one.
Each subject has its own page on the site: objective, possible research question, data, deliverables, tools listed in the syllabus, step-by-step approach and starter code.

lignes: Polarity of texts: positive, negative or neutral
Logistic regression: estimating an outcome (yes or no)
diapos.legende: Details of each subject on the site’s “Mini-project” page.
diapos.notes: Reassure the students: the methods will be covered in chapter 3, during the mini-project, and each subject page provides starter code. The syllabus lists both sklearn and scikit-learn: they are the same library. For subject 1, Tweepy is hardly usable (the X API has been paid since 2023), and GeoPandas is only useful if the texts are linked to a place.

diapos.question: “Can we see the fragmented structure of *Nedjma* in the network of its characters?” Which subject does this research question belong to?
diapos.explication: The characters are the nodes and their shared appearances the links; centrality measures show who connects the groups and who stays on the margins.
diapos.notes: Then read the other questions suggested on the site. Subject 1: how did internet users receive the film or TV adaptation of a novel? Subject 2: are there distinct reader profiles among Master’s students? Subject 3: which themes and which places dominate the speeches of the UN general debate? Subject 4: which factors are associated with students’ attendance at cultural events? Each group can draw on them, but must formulate its own question.

lignes: Sentiment140, Allociné, LABR; public comments collected by hand
Your anonymous questionnaire; World Values Survey, Arab Barometer
Official websites, vie-publique.fr, UN General Debate Corpus
Your questionnaire (a yes/no question); UCI public datasets
A link table noted while reading; NetworkX sample networks
diapos.legende: For each dataset: who produced it, where, when, and how it was collected.
diapos.notes: A questionnaire (subjects 2 and 4) requires the respondents’ consent and anonymity, and it takes time for people to fill it in: it must go out in the first week. With only a few dozen answers, conclusions remain very cautious. For subject 5, *Nedjma* is protected by copyright: share the link tables, not the digitized text. If a source seems uncertain to you, plan a small dataset to provide.

diapos.titre: Assigning the subjects to the six groups
consignes: Each group rereads the five subjects on the site and picks three, in order of preference.
Criteria: an interesting question, accessible data, the group’s equipment.
The spokesperson announces the three choices; the teacher arbitrates on the board.
Each group writes down its subject and a first idea for a research question.
diapos.materiel: The site’s “Mini-project” page (phone or computer room); the grid on the next slide
diapos.notes: A suggested procedure, not a rule of the syllabus: adapt it. Six groups for five subjects: with the one-subject rule, one subject will be taken by two groups, who can choose different corpora and compare their results in the oral presentation. With the three-subject rule, each group picks three and you make sure they are balanced. Equipment: subjects 1 and 3 require heavy libraries (transformers, torch, spaCy) and a good connection; subject 5 requires installing Gephi separately. A group without a computer can work in Colab or in the computer room.

diapos.legende: A grid to copy onto the board or to print; each row is approved by the teacher during the first week.
diapos.notes: Fill in the grid on the board during the arbitration, then post it in the class space (Moodle or messaging group): it becomes the shared reference. The PDF export of the slideshow also lets you print it blank.

points: Rotating roles: secretary, spokesperson, timekeeper
The less confident student at the keyboard; the other guides, and you swap regularly
A dated **logbook**: what you tried, what failed, what you decided and why
Every member can explain any cell of the notebook
Progress is shown to the teacher every week
diapos.notes: These tips come from the guide and from the “Study method” page. For group work, the guide suggests marking the code and the report collectively, and the oral presentation individually: each member answers a question on a part they did not present. If you adopt this principle, announce it today: it prevents a single student from writing all the code.
The approach is the same for all subjects; each subject page then details it step by step.

etapes.titre: W1 · Choose and define the scope
etapes.texte: A precise research question, one or two hypotheses, approved by the teacher.
Collect, write a source sheet, anonymize, load into a pandas table.
Count, sort, find duplicates and missing values; write down each decision.
The subject’s tool or algorithm, checked on a small sample that you read yourself.
Go back to the texts or the data; identify biases and limitations.
Write the report, rerun the whole notebook, prepare the oral presentation.

diapos.notes: W1, W2 and W3 are the three weeks of the mini-project. Advice from the “Study method” page: start small; a corpus of fifty texts that works is better than ten thousand that do not. The step most often forgotten is checking on a sample read by hand: insist on it.

points: **Sources**: who produced the data, where, when, how it was collected
**Privacy**: remove names, usernames and identifiers; respondents’ consent
**Rights**: terms of use and copyright; analyzing is not republishing
**Reproducibility**: another person can rerun the notebook and get the same results
**Transparency**: any use of an AI assistant is declared, and everything it produces is checked
diapos.notes: These five rules appear on the mini-project page and apply to all subjects. Privacy: in Algeria, Law No. 18-07 of 10 June 2018 governs the processing of personal data. Rights: a recent novel may be analyzed, but not republished online. Transparency: the guide suggests ending each report with a declaration of use of AI tools (tool, date, use, prompts, checking), even if the answer is “none”.

evenements.texte: End of chapter 2: the mini-project is handed out
Define the scope, gather the data; research questions approved
Explore, clean, apply the method; progress check
Interpret, write up; submit the notebook and the report

diapos.notes: This is the schedule that the guide suggests over thirteen weeks, for the one-subject rule. Only the handing out at the end of chapter 2 and the three-week duration come from the syllabus. Replace the week numbers with the dates of your faculty’s calendar, and announce the due date, how the work is submitted and the length of the oral presentation. With three subjects, spread them from week 4 to week 9.

diapos.sousTitre: What you hand in, and how it will be assessed
diapos.notes: Hand out the assessment grid today, together with the assignment: that way, the students know what counts.

lignes: Runs without errors from start to finish after a kernel restart
Attached to the notebook, or how to obtain them explained precisely
Question, data, method, results, interpretation, limitations
Numbered, given a title and discussed in the text of the report
Your question, your main result, one limitation of your approach
diapos.legende: Due date, length of the oral presentation and how to submit: set by the teacher.
diapos.notes: A Jupyter notebook mixes code cells, results and explanatory text. Suggested outline for the report: research question, data, method, results, interpretation, limitations and ethical issues, references. Each subject adds its own deliverables, specified on its page: a hand-annotated sample (subject 1), a variable dictionary (subject 2), a table of entities (subject 3), a comparison with a naive model (subject 4), a GEXF file (subject 5).

points: Present your question, your main result and one limitation of your approach
“Show the cell that cleans the data and explain each line.”
“Change k = 3 to k = 4 in front of me: what changes?”
“Name three messages that your model misclassified and explain each error.”
diapos.notes: The last three lines are examples of questions that the guide suggests for the oral presentation: only the author of a piece of work can answer them, which makes the oral presentation more convincing than a detector of generated text. Warn the students today: it is the best incentive to understand every line of their notebook. The length of the oral presentation is for you to set.

lignes: Precise, linked to SHS or to literature, feasible in three weeks
Source, date, collection given; anonymization and cleaning described
Runs from start to finish; code commented; parameters given
Charts with titles and comments; return to the texts or the data
Recommended outline followed, 4 to 6 pages, complete references
Keeps to time, explains a code cell and a limitation
diapos.legende: A suggested marking scheme from the guide; official grading follows the regulations in force. Before handing in your work, review it with the site’s self-assessment grid.
diapos.notes: The syllabus only says “Evaluation (identical to the regulations in force)”: do not announce any percentage that your faculty has not set, and scale these points to the share that the regulations give the mini-project. The other levels (insufficient, fair, very good) are in the guide, under “Assessing students”.

points: A mere topic: “feelings on Facebook”
Data without a source, or not anonymized
A notebook that does not run from start to finish
Figures and charts without comment
A precise question, with a hypothesis to discuss
A source sheet; anonymized data
Rerun the whole notebook before handing it in
Go back to the texts to interpret the figures

diapos.notes: The left column reflects the “insufficient” level of the grid, the right column the “good” and “very good” levels. Ask each group which of these pitfalls threatens it most, given its subject.

points: Read the whole page of your subject
Formulate a research question and one or two hypotheses
Find an accessible data source and start the source sheet
Start the logbook
diapos.texte: The scope of each group’s project is approved by the teacher during the first week.
diapos.notes: Set the time for approving the scope (lab session (TP) or appointment) and remind the students of the class’s single channel for questions. If a group is preparing a questionnaire, ask to see it before it is sent out: consent and anonymity must be included.
